content: Rimantadine is a medication prescribed to prevent and treat infections caused by the influenza A virus. It may also be prescribed for other purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Rimantadine is available in tablet and liquid forms, which are taken orally. It is typically taken once or twice daily for a duration of 2 to 12 weeks. A flu vaccine will also be administered alongside this medication. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take rimantadine exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less of it, and do not take it more frequently than directed by your doctor. Before starting rimantadine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rimantadine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including acetaminophen, aspirin, cimetidine (Tagamet), and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, seizures, or blood disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking rimantadine, contact your doctor immediately. Rimantadine may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose of rimantadine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Rimantadine may cause mild side effects. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Upset stomach Nervousness Fatigue Difficulty sleeping or concentrating Lightheadedness In rare cases, rimantadine may cause severe side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Skin rash Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) Mood changes Mental confusion Vision changes If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store rimantadine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any required laboratory tests. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to rimantadine. Do not share this medication with anyone else. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of rimantadine, contact your doctor. Rimantadine is sold under the brand names Flumadine® and Flumadine® Syrup.
